notes: What the app gets wrong today. Each entry prints as KNOWN on every run and does not fail it. An entry that stops matching fails the run until it is taken off the list, so a fix is always noticed. The contrast entries are one per screen, theme and color pair, each with the ratio the app draws. The language entries are one per kind of word the API cannot send in Spanish yet, which stay until it does, and one per place the portal itself still draws English, which the build that fixes it takes off. A too small entry names the control and why it is under 44 today.

failures.what: is a to-do item the API sent in English
failures.why: A to-do item and its instructions are written in English in the database and the API sends them as written. The API's build gives them Spanish and sends the language the request asks for.

failures.why: A to-do item's zone is written in English in the database and sent as written, the same as the item.

failures.why: An in-app notice is written by the API in English at the moment it is sent. The API's build writes it in the person's saved language.

failures.what: is a Help reply the API sent in English
failures.why: Help's replies, the fixed ones included, arrive from the API in English. The route already carries the language; the reply's language is the API's to change.

failures.what: is a procedure name the API sent in English
failures.why: The procedures an answer cites are named the way the API writes them, in English. Their names are the API's to send in the person's language, with Help's replies. The suite draws one for the first time in this build.

failures.where: Every notice type on the bell
failures.check: a support_ticket notice opens a place of its own in the portal
failures.what: the tap is marked read and left on the bell
failures.why: A support_ticket notice has no place in the portal: NOTIF_TAB (src/App.js:10898-10941) has no entry for it and notifPlace (src/App.js:10975-10982) answers null, so a tap only marks it read and leaves the bell open. Contract 2.6 says a notice tap opens the item itself. Findings: notices that open nothing.

failures.check: a check-off is kept on the phone (the API answering 500)
failures.why: A check-off that meets a 500 (or a 502 or 503 while Railway replaces its one container) is not kept: toggleTask keeps a tap only for ERR_OFFLINE or auth.mustSetPin (src/App.js:2566), so the box goes back and a 3-second toast is all the cleaner sees. A queued tap that meets one later is deleted (src/App.js:2591-2597).

failures.check: an uncheck is kept on the phone (the API answering 500)
failures.why: The same as a check-off: an uncheck that meets a 500 is not kept (src/App.js:2566).

failures.check: End Shift goes by itself once the signal is back (the signal gone as the tap is made)
failures.why: End Shift with no signal shows a toast and keeps nothing (src/App.js:2483-2510); the end is sent only when the person taps again with signal, and it sends no time of its own (src/App.js:2492), so the shift ends when the request arrives.

failures.where: Weak signal: an issue with a photo
failures.check: an issue with a photo is kept on the phone (the API answering 500)
failures.why: submitIssue catches its own error and returns (src/App.js:2662), and handleSubmit then clears the title, details, zone and photo and closes the form (src/App.js:7696), so the report is gone when the send fails. With a photo, a drop at the photo's upload keeps the form, since uploadPhoto throws first.
